blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Vancouver Heights. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Vancouver Heights, Burnaby: 22 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 1 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 5%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 11 of 35 Burnaby communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Vancouver Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

15 condos sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $565,000 (the middle half sold between $491,500 and $976,900), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $790 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $397 a month. 5 townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $835,000, taking a median of 25 days to sell at 98.0% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $794 per square foot, a median year built of 2003 and a median strata fee of $470 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Vancouver Heights

TOP FLAG — THE NAME LIES, AND THE MAP HAS THREE TRAPS. Vancouver Heights is in the City of Burnaby (North Burnaby, on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine) — not the City of Vancouver, despite the name. This pass verified 4 apartment-condo buildings by name on building-directory plus listing evidence; three more named buildings (The Mondeo, Verdi, Carleton Terrace) rest on listing evidence only and are carried UNVERIFIED, not counted. Tenure trap: Seton Villa Retirement Centre (3755 McGill St) is the sub-area's only verified seniors building and it is rental/care — nothing to buy; the 55+ program verified zero 55+ ownership here. Checked and out-of-area: Burnaby Hospital is at 3935 Kincaid St, south across the city — not in-area. Contact check: this area has no live page on jaredgibbons.ca, so no instance of jared@jaredgibbons.ca was found (no live page exists); the correct contact email is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca.
The Sienna — 3939 Hastings Street

A 22-unit strata building: the building directory records it built in 1998, with bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" and amenities of air conditioning, central air, garden and private yard — the rental-restriction element of that directory line is VOID since November 24, 2022. Current listings record the subdivision name "The Sienna," Area Minor Vancouver Heights, Apartment/Condo form and a 1998 build year, consistent with the directory. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus name-verifying current listings. Counted: 1.
The Carleton (listing subdivision name "Carleton") — 4223 Hastings Street

No standalone directory FAQ page for the building was surfaced this pass — the directory evidence is the directory site's own building records for the address, stated as such. No rental, pet or age restriction is stated for it in the sources checked — UNCONFIRMED per the Form B. Counted: 1.
Heritage Green — 3978 Albert Street

The building directory records Heritage Green built in 1994 with 28 units, in-suite laundry, and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental-restriction element is VOID since November 24, 2022; the directory records an active listing at the address, and a unit at 3978 Albert Street is carried in the Vancouver Heights MLS listings index. The directory's unit filters for this address also show a townhouse variant, so a given unit's form is UNCONFIRMED until checked against the strata plan — the building is counted on its apartment units. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus listing evidence at the address. Counted: 1.
Evergreen Place — 3861 Albert Street

The building directory records Evergreen Place built in 1989, with in-suite laundry and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental-restriction element is VOID since November 24, 2022 — and records the building's listing and sale history at this address, most recently in October 2025; no unit was actively listed at the check. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus the directory's recorded listing history at the address. Counted: 1.
Streets, schools and getting around Vancouver Heights

items.t: Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in North Burnaby, on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine; "Vancouver Heights" is the MLS (GVR board) sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The neighbourhood frame in the 55+ notes is Boundary Road west, Gamma Avenue east, Hastings Street south and Burrard Inlet north. West of Boundary Road is the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) — a different municipality, different sub-area.

Where condo stock concentrates: low-rise strata buildings on Hastings Street itself and one block north on Albert Street. The rest of the sub-area is predominantly detached houses on a sloping, view-oriented hillside — early-to-mid-20th-century homes, post-war bungalows and Vancouver Special-era houses alongside newer rebuilds. Strata product is concentrated on/near Hastings.

Community (Burnaby; medians are published at community level only) — detached median $1,825,000, $662/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 37 days on market; condos & townhomes median $686,000, $763/sq ft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market. Twelve-month community trend: the detached median ranged from $1,750,000 (June 2026) to $1,992,500 (December 2025), ending at $1,825,000; the attached median ranged from $643,250 (July 2026) to $720,000 (October 2025), ending at $686,000. No sub-area median is published — sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings Street through the Heights, linking Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak, with in-area stops including Hythe, Holdom and Kensington. On September 7, 2026, TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving the Heights with peak service every 6–7 minutes and replacing the peak-only 222 bus. There is no SkyTrain station in this sub-area.

Schools and catchments (SD41, Burnaby): two elementary schools sit on Pandora Street inside the sub-area — Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora St) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora St) — and the locator splits the street by address range: 4375 Pandora St → Rosser Elementary / Alpha Secondary; 4715 Pandora St → Confederation Park Elementary / Alpha Secondary. Burnaby North Secondary (751 Hammarskjold Dr) is located in North Burnaby but was NOT the locator result for either sample address — location is not catchment; state it plainly and run the exact address.

Parks, recreation and civic: Confederation Park (250 Willingdon Ave), Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre (240 Willingdon Ave) and the McGill Branch of Burnaby Public Library (4595 Albert St) form the west-end civic cluster; Capitol Hill Reservoir Park (229 N Hythe Ave) is listed by the City as a scenic viewpoint park. The City's planned new Confederation Park Community Centre beside the pool and library has been deferred by the City. In August 2026 the Province announced funding for 20 new child-care spaces at Confederation Park Elementary.
Health care: there is no hospital in the sub-area; Burnaby Hospital is at 3935 Kincaid St, south across the city — checked, and out-of-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Vancouver Heights

items.t: Two near-identical building names sit five blocks apart on the same street. The Sienna (3939 Hastings St) is a 1998 resale building of 22 units, counted in; Siena (4451 Hastings St) is a 38-residence presale by Landa Global with a spring 2028 completion. A search, a showing request or an offer that drops one letter lands on the wrong building.

The building called "The Heights" is not filed in Vancouver Heights. The Heights (3768 Hastings St, 1998, 37 units) carries this neighbourhood's name, but its own MLS listing record files it under the Willingdon Heights sub-area — it stands on the south side of Hastings at the west edge.
Carleton appears twice, too. Confirm the street address, not just the name, before booking a showing.

One street, two elementary schools — and the "obvious" secondary is wrong. Pandora Street carries both in-area elementaries, and the SD41 locator splits it by address range: 4375 Pandora St → Rosser Elementary, 4715 Pandora St → Confederation Park Elementary, both feeding Alpha Secondary in the runs recorded — not Burnaby North Secondary, the school physically located in North Burnaby. Repeating a school name without running the address is an error waiting to happen.
Detached sold briskly while attached barely moved. Price an attached unit against the attached evidence, not the hillside's detached headline. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

Burnaby replaced both of its governing documents within seven months. The Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) replaced the 1998 OCP, and the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, in effect July 1, 2026) replaced the 1965 zoning bylaw — and the new OCP takes precedence over the older neighbourhood community-plan maps, including for the Hastings corridor's Heights Urban Village. Any Heights document or old listing citing the 1965 bylaw or the 1998 OCP as current is out of date twice over.
The seniors tower stands on a heritage estate. The tower itself opened in 1974 and is rental/care: it anchors the area's seniors services without adding a single buyable unit.
The claim that Brentwood is the nearest enclosed mall is UNVERIFIED — the Heights' own shopping is the Hastings street-front strip, and no source checked states the mall claim as fact.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Vancouver Heights
Streets, schools and getting around Vancouver Heights

items.t: Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in northwest Burnaby (North Burnaby), on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine; the MLS® sub-area name (GVR board) is "Vancouver Heights." Nearby areas: Capitol Hill (the hilltop portion within/adjacent to this sub-area), Willingdon Heights, Parkcrest, Lochdale, Westridge, Burnaby Heights to the west, and the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) across Boundary Road.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: it does not form complexes here. No named townhouse complex inside the sub-area was verified in the research, the condos pass, the 55-plus pass or this pass.
SnapStats publishes no Vancouver Heights sub-area median.

Plan and zoning frame: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP Bylaw) governs and takes precedence over older neighbourhood community-plan maps where they conflict; the Hastings corridor is planned as the Heights Urban Village, with mixed-use redevelopment proposals processed along Hastings (for example at 4472 Hastings Street at Willingdon Avenue). Zoning is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026) — never the former 1965 Bylaw No. 4742. Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District (June 2024) applies to nearly every residential lot here: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.

Schools (SD41; Ministry-listed names only) — settled chain cited: the SD41 locator run documented in the research for the sample in-area address 4375 Pandora St (locator range 4303–4375 PANDORA ST) returned Rosser Elementary (K–7) / Alpha Secondary (8–12) (SD41 School Locator, run 2026-11-01). Vancouver Heights catchment = Alpha Secondary for that address range. Two SD41 elementary schools sit on Pandora Street inside the sub-area — Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora St) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora St) — and the Capitol Hill sample (4715 Pandora St) returned Confederation Park Elementary / Alpha Secondary, so the two in-area Pandora elementaries split the street by address range while the secondary stays Alpha. Burnaby North Secondary (751 Hammarskjold Drive) is the other secondary school located in North Burnaby — location is not catchment. Catchments for other Heights addresses: UNVERIFIED.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings through the Heights (Burrard Station to SFU; at least every 10 minutes at peak, 15 minutes off-peak; stops include Hythe, Holdom and Kensington). On September 7, 2026, TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving Burnaby Heights with peak service every six to seven minutes and replacing the peak-only 222 bus.

Anchors: Confederation Park (250 Willingdon Avenue — one of Burnaby's largest parks, with the cenotaph for North Burnaby's Remembrance Day ceremony), the Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre (240 Willingdon Avenue), the McGill Branch of Burnaby Public Library (4595 Albert Street), and Capitol Hill Reservoir Park (229 N Hythe Avenue), a scenic viewpoint park at the top of Capitol Hill. A new Confederation Park Community Centre beside the pool and library is a City capital project whose replacement project has been deferred.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Vancouver Heights

items.t: Form B diligence (strata frame): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a Heritage Green unit marketed as a "townhouse," the Form B and strata plan are what settle the unit's form — the directory's townhouse-variant filter does not.

SSMUH on house lots: under the R1 SSMUH District, most Heights lots allow 3–6 homes (6 only within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop) and multi-unit product may be stratified — so two otherwise similar houses can be worth very different amounts to builders depending on lot area and the 400 m transit test (the R5/R2 Hastings corridor makes that test live on many lots). Review the Burnaby 2050 OCP land use map and the Heights Urban Village direction before assuming redevelopment or assembly value on Hastings-fronting and near-Hastings properties, because the new OCP takes precedence over older community plan maps.

No Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in Burnaby — the name trap, stated expressly: the EHT is a City of Vancouver tax (3% of assessed value) and it does not apply in Vancouver Heights, because Vancouver Heights is in Burnaby. A buyer importing a Vancouver tax checklist on the strength of the name will budget a tax that does not exist here. The provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax is its own regime and is not the EHT.

City property taxes (2026): City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Vancouver Heights

items.t: The civic cluster is mid-replacement — and deferred. The new Confederation Park Community Centre would retain the McGill Branch library (built 2001) and Eileen Dailly pool (built 1992) and replace the 1971 seniors centre — but the City states the replacement project has been deferred, so the 1971-vintage centre remains the operating fact.

The park is also the war memorial. Confederation Park hosts the cenotaph where North Burnaby's Remembrance Day ceremony is held — the sub-area's civic anchor is a park, a pool, a library and a memorial in one cluster at Willingdon and Albert.

Childcare arrived by repurposing a school. In August 2026 the Province announced funding to repurpose school space at Confederation Park Elementary for 20 new before- and after-school child care spaces — an in-area school gaining a second use, worth knowing on a street whose two elementaries split the catchment.

The view is the lot, street by street. Capitol Hill's upper streets are known for views over Burrard Inlet, downtown Vancouver and the North Shore mountains, and view premium and sun exposure change street by street on the slope — with detached turnover at 38% in September 2026, pricing the view correctly is the whole game on the hill.
The "Heights" brand crosses the sub-area line. A Heights buyer's comparable set changes depending on which side of the filing line a building sits.

Zero townhome complexes is a verified finding, not a missing search. The Heights' ground-oriented supply is the detached house — which is exactly why its R1 multiplex potential, not a townhouse complex, is the ground-oriented conversation here.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 22 condos and townhomes listed in Vancouver Heights. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Vancouver Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Vancouver Heights had a sales ratio of 5%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 7 condos and townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights over those 4 months, out of 750 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Vancouver Heights sell for?
faq.a: 15 condos sold in Vancouver Heights between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $565,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: The median was 26 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.9% of the last list price (7% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

No — it is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in North Burnaby, east of Boundary Road, on and below the Capitol Hill rise. The City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) is across Boundary Road to the west. Burnaby taxes, Burnaby bylaws, School District 41 and Burnaby market statistics apply — and there is no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax here.

faq.q: Where are the condos, and which buildings are verified by name?
faq.a: On and just off Hastings Street: four counted buildings — The Sienna (3939 Hastings St, 1998, 22 units), The Carleton (4223 Hastings St, 2020, 22 units), Heritage Green (3978 Albert St, 1994, 28 units) and Evergreen Place (3861 Albert St, 1989). Three more named buildings — The Mondeo (3811 Hastings St), Verdi (3971 Hastings St) and Carleton Terrace (4160 Albert St) — appear in listings only and are carried UNVERIFIED, not counted.

faq.q: How did Vancouver Heights sell in September 2026?
faq.a: SnapStats publishes no Vancouver Heights median — sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: Can I buy a suite at Seton Villa?
faq.a: No. Seton Villa (3755 McGill St) is a 19-storey non-profit retirement centre operated by Action Line Housing Society, registered in BC's Assisted Living Registry — independent/supportive suites and assisted living that you rent into or are placed into. There is no strata ownership to purchase, and it is the sub-area's only verified seniors building; there is no verified 55+ ownership stock here.

faq.q: Which secondary school serves the Heights — Burnaby North?
faq.a: Not on the locator evidence. SD41 locator runs for two in-area Pandora Street addresses (4375 and 4715 Pandora St) both returned Alpha Secondary, with Rosser Elementary for the first and Confederation Park Elementary for the second. Burnaby North Secondary (751 Hammarskjold Dr) is located in North Burnaby, but location is not catchment. Run the exact address before writing an offer.

No — Burnaby. Despite the name, Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in North Burnaby, east of Boundary Road; its market statistics are reported under Burnaby in the SnapStats GVR report, and Burnaby's taxes, bylaws and school district (SD41) apply — including no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax.

faq.q: A Heritage Green unit is marketed as a townhouse — is it one?
faq.a: The building is counted on its apartment units; the directory's unit filters for 3978 Albert Street also show a townhouse variant, so a given unit's form is UNCONFIRMED until checked against the strata plan. Either way the unit is a strata lot in that apartment development — condo-program stock, not a townhouse complex. Read the Form B.

faq.q: Which secondary school serves the Heights — Alpha or Burnaby North?
faq.a: Alpha Secondary, on the settled SD41 locator chain: the run for 4375 Pandora St returned Rosser Elementary / Alpha Secondary, and the Capitol Hill sample on the same street (4715 Pandora St) also returned Alpha Secondary. Burnaby North Secondary is located in North Burnaby but is not the catchment secondary for those Pandora addresses. Other addresses: UNVERIFIED — catchments do not follow MLS sub-area lines, so run the specific address.
